record.name: Aged Northern Vietnam Ripe Pu-erh Tea
record.origin: Northern Vietnam highlands, on the Yunnan border, Vietnam

paragraphs.text: This loose leaf comes from the [northern Vietnam highlands](northern-vietnam-highlands:where-it-is), the high, misty mountain provinces along the border with China. Many of the groves there are old [Shan Tuyet](northern-vietnam-highlands:old-trees) trees, a family of large-leaf tea trees named snow mountain for the fine white down on their buds, and Mông and Dao communities look after many of them. The hills share Yunnan's large-leaf trees, climate and forest just over the border, which is why the trade [sets this leaf beside pu'er](northern-vietnam-highlands:beside-yunnan), though it remains a tea of its own country.

Here it was made as [ripe tea](northern-vietnam-highlands:ripe-tea), as old-tree leaf in these highlands mostly is in Ha Giang. In [ripe pu'er](shou:definition) making the leaf is heaped warm and damp in a [fermenting pile](shou:wet-piling), covered to hold in the heat the microbes make and turned to let air in, so that it reaches in weeks a change raw leaf takes years to make. Whether such tea may carry the [pu'er name](northern-vietnam-highlands:on-a-label) is not agreed: many keep the name for Yunnan, and some sellers call it a Vietnamese dark tea made in the pu'er style.

brewing.text: Ripe pu’er takes boiling water: fermented, tightly packed leaf needs full heat to open, and it does not scald the way green tea can. A common start is about 7 grams to 100 ml and one quick rinse, which wakes the leaf and carries off dust and any pile smell. Then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens, so the cup stays clear rather than heavy; it gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, sweet cup with earthy or woody notes. A young ripe tea can carry a faint smell of the pile, which fades with airing or in the first steeps.

unsupported.sentence: Here it was made as [ripe tea](northern-vietnam-highlands:ripe-tea), as old-tree leaf in these highlands mostly is in Ha Giang.
unsupported.words: as old-tree leaf in these highlands mostly is in Ha Giang
unsupported.why: The claim says ripe tea is made here from old-tree leaf, mostly in Ha Giang. That tells us where most ripe tea is made. It does not say that most old-tree leaf in the highlands, or in Ha Giang, is made into ripe tea. The sentence turns the claim around and states something it does not support.
